Reviewed the branch behind that trail (`fix/1928-agent-group-external-discovery`, 17 commits, 8 files). Build, `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/...` and the targeted `cli` tests pass; golangci-lint v2.11.3 reports 0 issues.

## Overall

The shape is right. `ListAvailable()` as the single place the test-only filter lives, with `StringList` as a thin name projection, removes the three copies of that filter (registry, `setup.hookAgentOptions`, list rendering). The `Get` locking change is correct — the RLock is released before `StringList` re-enters, so there's no nested-RLock/writer-starvation deadlock, and the inner `Get` calls only hit registered names so the recursion terminates. `SnapshotForTesting` is a genuinely good addition: mock agents backed by `t.TempDir` binaries leaking into the process-global registry is exactly the kind of cross-test corruption that shows up as an unrelated flake later. `TestRunAgentList_DefaultPathDoesNotScanPath` proving the fast path never execs via an exec log is the right way to pin that property.

## Worth addressing

**1. The headline fix is the untested part.** `agent list --external` has nine tests; `agent add <external-name>` and `agent remove <external-name>` — the actual "1928" fix, and the two places that call `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` — have none. Nothing covers: a plugin on PATH resolving through `add`, the wrapped error (`loading external agent %q: %w`) when the binary is found but fails to load, or the unknown-name fallthrough to `printWrongAgentError`. The machinery already exists (`writeExternalAgentBinaryEx` + a temp PATH dir), so this is cheap.

**2. Default `agent list` can't see an installed external agent.** `cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go:79` — with hooks installed for an external plugin, plain `entire agent list` skips it *and* prints "No built-in agents installed." The wording is technically accurate and the footer hint points at `--external`, but a user whose only active agent is external sees a listing that looks like nothing is set up. An earlier commit on this branch (`896e533f`) did show installed externals by default before being replaced — worth confirming that reversal was deliberate rather than a casualty of the `--all` → `--external` rework.

**3. "One answer to which agents are available" isn't quite complete.** `cmd/entire/cli/review/cmd.go:560` (`availableReviewAgents`) still builds a user-facing picker catalog from `agent.List()`, i.e. test-only included. It's safe today only because no reviewer is registered for vogon, so `reviewerFor` filters it incidentally. The other remaining `List()` callers (`removeAgentHooks`, `detectAgentByTranscript`, discovery's conflict set) correctly want everything.

## Nits

- `agent.Get` on a miss now resolves *every* registered agent just to build the error string, and `discoverAndRegisterNamed` uses `Get` as an existence probe (`external/discovery.go:93`) — so `entire agent add <typo>` pays that twice. Free today since external factories return a cached value, but an `IsRegistered(name) bool` would make the probe honest.
- `printAgentError` unconditionally appends "External agent plugins on your PATH are also available: run 'entire agent list --external'". On the `agent add`/`remove` path the CLI just looked up that exact name on PATH and didn't find it, so the hint reads as if a search is still pending.
- `runAgentList` re-implements `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled`'s loop inline. Justified (it needs the `Agent` value for `IsExternal`), but the two will drift; `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` could take the `ListAvailable` result now that one exists.

`entire agent add/list/remove` omitted external agents (e.g. `zed`), failing with `Unknown agent`, even though `entire enable --agent <name>` and the git-hook paths worked. The `agent` noun-group never invoked external-agent discovery, so `agent.Get` / `agent.List` only saw statically-registered built-ins.

Fixes #1928.

## Changes
- `add` / `remove` `RunE`: resolve the single named plugin via `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, name)` before `agent.Get` / `runRemoveAgent`. Targeting the exact name (rather than a full `$PATH` scan) avoids executing every unrelated `entire-agent-*` binary, and surfaces a real plugin load error instead of a generic "unknown agent". Built-in names short-circuit instantly (no exec); an unknown name still falls through to `printWrongAgentError`. These bypass the `external_agents` gate because the action is itself the opt-in — and `add` auto-persists `external_agents=true` for an external agent (via `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`).
- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`. A footer points at `--external`.
- **`--external`** is a **superset**: it lists the built-in agents *and* the external plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available) via full discovery, reusing the built-in rendering — same `Agents:` header, installed `✓` marker, and test-only filter — so output is uniform. External entries carry an `(external)` suffix, because they are arbitrary executables resolved from `$PATH` rather than code shipped in the binary, and that distinction is trust-relevant.
  - This replaces the earlier `--all` flag. Previously the default path executed every plugin on `$PATH` to mark installed externals — a per-plugin exec cost that scaled with plugin count on a sub-100ms command. All external work is now behind the explicit `--external` opt-in.
- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.
- **`printAgentError` (the "Unknown agent" / "Missing agent name" path) no longer contradicts `agent list`**:
  - It goes through the new `agent.ListAvailable`, so test-only agents (`vogon`) are no longer advertised as available.
  - It does not scan `$PATH` (the error path should stay cheap), so it now points at `entire agent list --external` — otherwise the user whose external plugin this PR just made addable gets an "Available agents" list that omits it after a single typo.
  - The usage line follows the caller's command surface (`entire agent add` / `entire agent remove` / `entire enable --agent`) instead of always printing `entire enable --agent`.

No inline test-only checks remain outside `registry.go`. It returns name+agent pairs because an external plugin's self-reported `Name()` is not validated against the registry key derived from its binary, and the registry key is the identity users type and `agent.Get` accepts.

fix: drop the external-plugin hint where the listing is already complete

is knowably incomplete. Full scan already ran => no hint. Targeted

open-ended pointer, which now has exactly one caller, the --agent
FlagErrorFunc that cobra runs before RunE and so before any discovery.
printMissingAgentError splits into pre/post-discovery wrappers because it
was reached from both sides of that line.

The existing unit test passed only because it hardcoded the hint and never
ran discovery; the new command-level test executes the real enable RunE
with a plugin on $PATH and fails against the old behavior.
